cues.speaker: PRESENTER
cues.text: This evening we’re delighted to welcome Dan Beagle, who’s just written a book on looking for and finding food in the wild. He’s going to tell us everything we need to know about picking wild mushrooms.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Thank you very much. Well, I need to start by talking about safety. You really need to know what you’re doing because some mushrooms are extremely poisonous. Having said that, once you know what to look for, it’s really worth doing for the amazing variety of mushrooms available – which you can’t get in the shops. But of course, you have to be very careful and that’s why I always say you should never consume mushrooms picked by friends or neighbours – always remember that some poisonous mushrooms look very similar to edible ones and it’s easy for people to get confused. The other thing to avoid is mushrooms growing beside busy roads for obvious reasons. But nothing beats the taste of freshly picked mushrooms – don’t forget that the ones in the shops are often several days old and past their best. Q11/12

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: There are certain ideas about wild mushrooms that it’s important to be aware of.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Don’t listen to people who tell you that it’s only OK to eat mushrooms that are pale or dull – this is completely untrue.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Some edible mushrooms are bright red, for example.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Personally, I prefer mushrooms cooked but it won’t do you any harm to eat them uncooked in salads – it’s not necessary to peel them.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Another thing you should remember is that you can’t tell if a mushroom is safe to eat by its smell – some of the most deadly mushrooms have no smell and taste quite nice, apparently.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Finally, just because deer or squirrels eat a particular mushroom doesn’t mean that you can.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Of course, mushroom picking is associated with the countryside but if you haven’t got a car, your local park can be a great place to start.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: There are usually a range of habitats where mushrooms grow, such as playing fields and wooded areas.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: But you need to be there first thing in the morning, as there’s likely be a lot of competition – not just from people but wildlife too.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: The deer often get the best mushrooms in my local park.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: If you’re a complete beginner, I wouldn’t recommend going alone or relying on photos in a book, even the one I’ve written!

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: There are some really good phone apps for identifying mushrooms, but you can’t always rely on getting a good signal in the middle of a wood.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: If possible, you should go with a group led by an expert – you’ll stay safe and learn a lot that way.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Conservation is a really important consideration and you must follow a few basic rules.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: You should never pick all the mushrooms in one area – collect only enough for your own needs.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Be very careful that you don’t trample on young mushrooms or other plants.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: And make sure you don’t pick any mushrooms that are endangered and protected by law.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: There’s been a decline in some varieties of wild mushrooms in this part of the country.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Restaurants are becoming more interested in locally sourced food like wild mushrooms, but the biggest problem is that so many new houses have been built in this area in the last ten years.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: And more water is being taken from rivers and reservoirs because of this, and mushroom habitats have been destroyed.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Anyway, a word of advice on storing mushrooms.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Collect them in a brown paper bag and as soon as you get home, put them in the fridge.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: They’ll be fine for a couple of days, but it’s best to cook them as soon as possible – after washing them really carefully first, of course.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: So everybody knows what a mushroom tastes like, right?

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Well, you’ll be surprised by the huge variety of wild mushrooms there are.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: Be adventurous!

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: They’re great in so many dishes – stir fries, risottos, pasta.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: But just be aware that some people can react badly to certain varieties so it’s a good idea not to eat huge quantities to begin with.

cues.speaker: DAN
cues.text: OK, so now I’m going to show you …
